preconditions.description: The number of test cases T is at least 1.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(M_str) <= 10**5 for M_str in M_strs)
preconditions.description: The length of each M_str is between 1 and 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(N_str) <= 10**5 for N_str in N_strs)
preconditions.description: The length of each N_str is between 1 and 10^5.

preconditions.expression: all(M_str.isdigit() and all(c in '01' for c in M_str) for M_str in M_strs)
preconditions.description: Each M_str consists only of '0' and '1'.

preconditions.expression: all(N_str.isdigit() and all(c in '01' for c in N_str) for N_str in N_strs)
preconditions.description: Each N_str consists only of '0' and '1'.
The number of queries Q is at least 1 for each test case.

preconditions.expression: all(all(1 <= x <= len(N_strs[i]) and 1 <= y <= len(M_strs[i]) for x, y in queries[i]) for i in range(len(queries)))
preconditions.description: Each query (x, y) satisfies 1 ≤ x ≤ N and 1 ≤ y ≤ M for the corresponding test case.

postconditions.description: The number of results matches the number of test cases T.

postconditions.expression: all(len(result) == Qs[i] for i, result in enumerate(results))
postconditions.description: Each result string has a length equal to the number of queries Q for the corresponding test case.

postconditions.expression: all(all(c in '01' for c in result) for result in results)
postconditions.description: Each result string consists only of '0' and '1'.

postconditions.expression: all(all((x, y) == (0, 0) or (x == 0 and M_strs[i][y-1] == result[j]) or (y == 0 and N_strs[i][x-1] == result[j]) for j, (x, y) in enumerate(queries[i])) for i, result in enumerate(results))
postconditions.description: Each result string correctly determines the winner for each query based on the terminal cell rules.
